items.title: BOJ decides Friday 18 September with no updated projections
items.detail: Because there is no refreshed outlook report at this meeting, the statement wording and the Governor's press conference carry the entire signal. A 25bp increase to 1.25% is fully priced; OIS carries almost a second hike by year-end and more than three by mid-2027.
items.decision: A hike itself is not the event. The vote split is — dissenters pushing for 50bp read hawkish, members preferring unchanged read dovish.

items.title: FOMC decides Wednesday 16 September with a new dot plot
items.detail: Market pricing for a 25bp hike lifted to roughly 90% after Friday's CPI. In June, nine of the eighteen forecast submissions saw at least one hike this year and six of those saw more than one — a marked turn from three months earlier, when the committee still projected the funds rate troughing near 3%.
items.decision: If both central banks hike, the differential is roughly unchanged and the trade lives entirely in the surprise, not the level.

items.title: Finance Minister Katayama again confirms close contact with Washington on currency
items.detail: Reported as a paraphrase, not a verbatim quote. Joint-action language is a distinct rung from unilateral escalation, and it is the rung that preceded the 3 August co-ordinated operation — the first US participation since 2011.
items.decision: No rung assigned. The desk does not score a paraphrase: the classifier needs the original wording, and the Observer's queue is where that gets captured.
items.source: StoneX, 12 Sep 2026, reporting remarks of 11 Sep

items.title: Twice rejected above 154.50; range floor at 152.90
items.detail: The post-CPI rally stalled above 154.50 and failed there for the second time since late last week. Below the 152.90 floor sits the January swing low at 152.10, then 151 — a level that has acted as both support and resistance for several years. RSI(14) around 29 with MACD extending after a bearish crossover.
items.decision: A close below 152.09 opens 151, the multi-year pivot. Above 154.50 the bearish structure is on hold, not broken.

items.title: Hot CPI, higher front-end yields — and the dollar fell anyway
items.detail: Core inflation came in above expectations, front-end yields rose and Fed pricing moved up, yet USD/JPY attempted a rally and then sold off sharply. The commentary attributes the behaviour to an unidentified force in the market.
items.decision: This is the signature of official-sector presence. Treat price action that contradicts the rate move as a flow question, not a macro one, until the monthly release settles it.

items.title: Record ¥15.4tn (≈ $100bn) deployment credited with marking the July top
items.detail: The single largest yen-buying operation on record. USD/JPY now trades around 6% below its July high, with the 100-week EMA nearby as support. A selloff matching the 13.8% that followed the July 2024 operation would imply materially lower levels; 15% would put the pair near 137.76.
items.decision: Size the tail, not the base case. The historical analogues argue the move does not stop where the intervention did.

items.title: 2 September yen surge: BOJ account data indicated no government intervention
items.detail: The move triggered widespread intervention speculation, but the central bank's account data subsequently showed no official operation behind it. Whether the ministry acted at any point after 2 September remains unconfirmed.
items.decision: The market moved without a yen being spent. That is the rate-check effect — and it is the cheapest form of intervention there is.
items.source: StoneX, Japanese Yen Outlook, 8 Sep 2026, citing Reuters and BOJ account data

items.title: Ministry monthly release on 30 September covers 27 Aug – 28 Sep
items.detail: This is the release that confirms or denies September intervention. Exact daily detail does not arrive until the quarterly breakdown in November.
items.decision: Diarised. This is the day the ladder gets graded against what was actually spent.
items.source: Japan Ministry of Finance disclosure schedule

items.title: United States joined yen intervention — first time since 2011
items.detail: Co-ordinated action of 3 August, with US participation, marked a structural change in what the ministry can credibly threaten. The US Treasury Secretary has since made unusually direct remarks, including describing himself as 'the house'.
items.decision: Joint action changes the payoff. A unilateral operation can be absorbed; a co-ordinated one cannot be faded on the same assumptions.
